package_info.package_versions: All versions where Trace.axd is enabled in production
package_info.why_malicious: When enabled in production environments, Trace.axd exposes sensitive diagnostic and session data—including plaintext credentials, session tokens, and internal application state—to unauthenticated users. This results in a critical information disclosure vulnerability that can be exploited for account takeover or further compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon HTTP request to /Trace.axd endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The Trace.axd handler processes incoming HTTP requests to the /Trace.axd endpoint and outputs detailed trace information for recent web requests. This includes session state, application state, request and response cookies, HTTP headers, and potentially POST body data, all displayed in plaintext to any user accessing the endpoint without authentication.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (ASP.NET built-in feature, not user code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when an unauthenticated HTTP request is made to /Trace.axd, the built-in handler collects and renders detailed diagnostic data—including session variables, cookies, HTTP headers, and recent request/response information—directly in the HTTP response, resulting in exposure of sensitive application and user data to the requester.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The handler exposes internal diagnostic and session data, including credentials and tokens, to any unauthenticated user accessing /Trace.axd. This enables attackers to obtain sensitive information that should be restricted to administrators.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard security practice is to restrict Trace.axd access to authenticated administrators or disable it entirely in production. The actual behavior allows public, unauthenticated access, violating the principle of least privilege and secure configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Trace.axd is legitimately used in development or staging environments for debugging and diagnostics by authorized developers. It should never be accessible in production or to unauthenticated users.
key_indicators: Trace.axd endpoint accessible without authentication in production
HTTP responses from /Trace.axd include session state, application state, and potentially plaintext credentials
Displays request and response cookies, HTTP headers, and POST body data
Reveals internal application structure, including physical directory paths and variable values

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers that the /Trace.axd endpoint is publicly accessible on the target ASP.NET application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to access and view recent web requests and diagnostic data without authentication.

attack_chain.action: Attacker inspects the trace logs for sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, session tokens, and internal application state variables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains credentials, session tokens, or other sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the exposed credentials or session tokens to impersonate users or escalate privileges within the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential account takeover, privilege escalation, or further compromise of the application and its users.

behavioral_signatures: Publicly accessible /Trace.axd endpoint responding to unauthenticated requests
Trace.axd HTTP responses containing session state, application state, or POST body data
Repeated unauthenticated access attempts to /Trace.axd from external or untrusted IP addresses
file_indicators: Presence of Trace.axd endpoint accessible in production environment
network_indicators: HTTP GET or POST requests to /Trace.axd from external or untrusted sources
Large HTTP responses from /Trace.axd containing diagnostic or session data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor production web servers for public access to /Trace.axd endpoints. Scan for the presence of Trace.axd and verify it is not accessible without authentication. Review web.config files for <trace enabled="true" /> settings. Alert on HTTP responses from /Trace.axd that include session state, credentials, or other sensitive data. Correlate repeated unauthenticated access attempts to /Trace.axd from external IPs as potential reconnaissance or exploitation activity.
